meta.description: Human-reviewed contributor queue. The bot reads this file and nothing else. Every entry is reviewed in a normal pull request, which is the point: an agent that decides at runtime what to build will duplicate, hallucinate, and file issues nobody can action.
notes: status: backlog    -> not eligible to be filed
status: ready      -> eligible; the bot may file it when the cap allows
status: filed      -> the bot created it; the marker lives in the issue body
status: shipped    -> the bot may comment + close its own issue, naming the release
Only entries with status=ready AND a complete body are ever filed.
latest_release   -> the tag the close comment cites; empty means the bot will not close anything it filed

items.title: docs: document the doctor and brain commands that already exist
items.body:
## Context

`package.json` already ships `doctor` (`node scripts/setup.js --check`) and `brain` (`node scripts/braincheck.js`), and the README mentions neither. A newcomer with a misconfigured model has no documented way to diagnose it.

## What to change

- `README.md`: after the install block, add `npm run doctor` and `npm run brain`, one line each on what they check.
- `docs/GUIDE.md`: add a "When something is wrong" subsection pointing at both.

Docs only; do not touch `src/` or `scripts/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `npm run doctor` appears in `README.md` and `docs/GUIDE.md`
- [ ] Both are described from real output you ran yourself
- [ ] `node --test` still passes

## How to verify

```bash
node scripts/setup.js --check
node scripts/braincheck.js
node --test
node scripts/audit.js
```

## Where to start

1. The "Install it in two commands" block near the top of `README.md`.
2. The configuration section of `docs/GUIDE.md`.

## Time estimate

~1-2 hours.

items.title: test(security): prove resolveInWorkspace() refuses a symlink escape
items.body:
## Context

`src/tools.js:90` defines `resolveInWorkspace()`, and the README makes a security claim about it: files are confined to `PINCH_WORKSPACE` through `realpath()`, so a symlink cannot walk out. That claim has no targeted regression test.

Run the case by hand first. If the guard does **not** hold, stop and report it privately per `SECURITY.md` instead of opening a public PR.

## What to change

- `test/hardening.test.js`: add a test that creates a temp workspace, plants a symlink pointing outside it, and asserts `resolveInWorkspace()` refuses the path.
- Use `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`. No new dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The test fails if `realpath()` confinement is removed (check by patching temporarily, then revert)
- [ ] Temp directory cleaned up in a `finally` block
- [ ] Passes on Node 22, 24 and 26
- [ ] Test name states the guarantee, not the implementation

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/hardening.test.js
node --test
node scripts/audit.js
```

## Where to start

1. `src/tools.js:90` - `resolveInWorkspace()`, about 30 lines.
2. `test/hardening.test.js` - copy the setup/teardown pattern from the nearest case.

## Time estimate

~2-3 hours.

items.title: test(cli): cover --version and an unknown verb in a smoke test
items.body:
## Context

`bin/pinch.js` is the entry point every user touches, and `scripts/growth.js` already carries a CLI-drift collector because promised verbs have drifted from implemented ones before. There is still no test that runs the CLI and asserts `--version` and an unknown verb behave sanely.

## What to change

- `test/cli.test.js` (new): via `node:child_process` `execFile` (argv array, never a shell string),
  1. `--version` exits 0 and prints the `package.json` version;
  2. an unknown verb exits non-zero or prints usage - assert whichever it does today and say which in the name;
  3. `help` prints a usage line containing a real verb.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No hard-coded version string; read it from `package.json`
- [ ] `execFile` with an argv array
- [ ] Passes on Node 22, 24, 26
- [ ] `node --test` still fully green

## How to verify

```bash
node bin/pinch.js --version
node bin/pinch.js help
node bin/pinch.js nope; echo "exit=$?"
node --test test/cli.test.js
```

## Where to start

1. `bin/pinch.js` - the verb `switch` and `usage()`.
2. `test/tools.test.js` - the existing spawn style.

## Time estimate

~2-3 hours.

items.title: feat(memory): search local conversation history across sessions
items.body:
## Context

`docs/CAPABILITIES.json` marks `conversation-search` as `missing` (`src/store.js` lists and loads sessions by ID, never searches them). Because Pinch keeps every session on disk as plain atomic JSON under `data/sessions/`, searching past conversations requires zero external dependencies.

## What to change

- `src/store.js`: add `searchSessions(query, { limit = 10 } = {})` returning matching turns (`{ sessionId, role, snippet, ts }`) sorted newest-first, confined strictly inside `data/sessions/`.
- `src/tools.js`: expose a read-only `search_history` tool (`dangerous: false`) that delegates to `searchSessions` and registers matched sessions in `src/sources.js` so citations stay verifiable.
- `test/batch2.test.js`: cover multi-session substring/case-insensitive search, empty-query refusal, and snippet truncation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `searchSessions()` reads only inside `data/sessions/` and returns bounded snippets (`<= 240` chars)
- [ ] `search_history` is non-dangerous (read-only) and requires zero external packages
- [ ] Empty or whitespace-only queries return an empty array without scanning disk
- [ ] Unit tests pass on Node 22, 24, and 26, and `node scripts/audit.js` stays green

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/batch2.test.js
node --test
node scripts/audit.js
```

## Where to start

1. `src/store.js` — inspect how sessions are listed and cached.
2. `src/tools.js` — follow the `recall` tool shape.

## Time estimate

~2-3 hours.

items.title: feat(telegram): preserve reply_to_message context in multi-turn chats
items.body:
## Context

`src/channels/telegram.js` polls `getUpdates` and routes `msg.text` directly to `routeMessage()`. When a user swipe-replies to an older Telegram message (`msg.reply_to_message`), that quoted text is dropped, so the assistant loses which message "do that again" or "summarize this" refers to.

## What to change

- `src/channels/telegram.js`: extract a pure helper `formatIncomingTelegramText(msg)` that prepends a bounded `[Replying to: "..."]\n` header (capped at 400 chars) when `msg.reply_to_message?.text` or `caption` is present, while leaving approval words (`yes`/`no`) untouched when replying to an approval prompt.
- `test/runtime.test.js`: add unit tests covering plain messages, quoted replies, oversized quoted text truncation, and approval replies.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Quoted Telegram replies include a bounded `[Replying to: ...]` prefix (`<= 400` chars)
- [ ] Replying `yes` or `no` to an approval prompt still resolves the pending approval cleanly
- [ ] Pure helper exported and tested without network calls
- [ ] `node --test` and `node scripts/audit.js` pass

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/runtime.test.js
node --test
node scripts/audit.js
```

## Where to start

1. `src/channels/telegram.js` — update loop around `routeMessage({ channel: "telegram", ... })`.
2. `src/channels/router.js` — check how `YES` / `NO` approval replies are matched.

## Time estimate

~2 hours.

items.title: feat(voice): validate audio uploads, enforce Whisper timeout, and report voice status in doctor
items.body:
## Context

`docs/CAPABILITIES.json` lists `voice` as `partial`: incoming audio works when `WHISPER_URL` is configured in `src/server.js`, but misconfigured or unreachable Whisper endpoints fail opaquely during phone voice use and `npm run doctor` (`scripts/setup.js --check`) does not report voice configuration status.

## What to change

- `src/server.js`: enforce a bounded timeout and supported audio MIME/size check on voice transcription requests, returning actionable JSON errors (`413` / `415` / `502` with clear message) when `WHISPER_URL` times out or is unset.
- `scripts/setup.js`: in `--check` (`npm run doctor`), report whether `WHISPER_URL` is configured and reachable (failing soft when unset, warning clearly when unreachable).
- `test/http-surface.test.js`: test unset `WHISPER_URL`, unsupported MIME, and upstream timeout handling.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Oversized or non-audio payloads are rejected with `413` / `415` before contacting `WHISPER_URL`
- [ ] Upstream Whisper hang aborts cleanly within a bounded deadline without crashing the server
- [ ] `node scripts/setup.js --check` reports voice configuration state accurately
- [ ] `node --test` and `node scripts/audit.js` pass

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/http-surface.test.js
node scripts/setup.js --check
node scripts/audit.js
```

## Where to start

1. `src/server.js` — search for `WHISPER_URL`.
2. `scripts/setup.js` — inspect the `--check` diagnostic output.

## Time estimate

~2-3 hours.

items.title: feat(brain): switch active local/cloud model at runtime without editing .env
items.body:
## Context

`docs/CAPABILITIES.json` marks `model-switching` as `partial`: `LLM_PROVIDER` and `OLLAMA_MODEL` are read once at boot, so switching between a fast local model and a coding/reasoning model requires editing `.env` and restarting Pinch.

## What to change

- `src/brain.js`: allow listing available Ollama models (`GET /api/tags`) and setting/reading the active runtime model override in memory (persisted optionally to `data/runtime.json` via `store.js`, never rewriting `.env`).
- `src/server.js`: expose `GET /api/models` and auth-guarded `POST /api/models` (`PINCH_KEY` / origin-checked).
- `src/channels/router.js`: support `/model` (show current + available) and `/model <name>` across Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, and web.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `/model` reports active provider and model; `/model <name>` switches subsequent turns without restart
- [ ] `POST /api/models` enforces the same auth/CSRF/host protections tested in `test/http-surface.test.js`
- [ ] `.env` is never modified on disk
- [ ] Update `docs/CAPABILITIES.json` `model-switching` evidence and add tests in `test/agent.test.js`

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/agent.test.js test/http-surface.test.js
node --test
node scripts/audit.js
```

## Where to start

1. `src/brain.js` — provider dispatch and model name resolution.
2. `src/channels/router.js` — command interception before `runAgent()`.

## Time estimate

~3-4 hours.

items.title: feat(personas): saved prompt presets and reusable personas in data/personas.json
items.body:
## Context

`docs/CAPABILITIES.json` marks `prompt-library` as `missing` (`src/prompt.js` builds one static persona at boot from `OWNER_NAME` and `PINCH_PROFILE`). Users want named local presets (e.g. concise coder, daily planner, strict reviewer) stored locally in `data/`.

## What to change

- `src/store.js` & `src/prompt.js`: load/save named persona overlays from `data/personas.json` using `atomicWrite()`, while keeping safety/guardrail system instructions non-overridable.
- `test/agent.test.js`: verify persona switching changes tone/instructions without bypassing `src/guard.js` or tool approval rules.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Personas persist atomically inside `data/personas.json` and are included in `pinch export`
- [ ] Core honesty/tool-approval instructions in `src/prompt.js` cannot be erased by a persona preset
- [ ] Covered by unit tests in `test/agent.test.js`

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/agent.test.js
node scripts/audit.js
```

## Time estimate

~2-3 hours.

items.title: chore(cli): prepare package.json for npm publish as pinch-ai without leaking local state
items.body:
## Context

The only install path today is `git clone`. `npm i -g pinch` belongs to an unrelated 2022 package, whereas `pinch-ai` provides a clean `npx pinch-ai setup` onboarding flow.

## What to change

- `package.json`: configure `files` allowlist (`bin/`, `src/`, `public/`, `scripts/setup.js`, `scripts/braincheck.js`, `LICENSE`, `README.md`) and `publishConfig.access: public`.
- `test/cli.test.js`: assert `npm pack --dry-run --json` never bundles `data/`, `test/`, `.github/`, or `.env` and stays under 1 MB.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `npm pack --dry-run` tarball contains no `data/`, `test/`, or `.env`
- [ ] Tarball size stays under 1 MB
- [ ] `node --test test/cli.test.js` enforces the allowlist invariant

## How to verify

```bash
npm pack --dry-run
node --test test/cli.test.js
node scripts/audit.js
```

## Time estimate

~2 hours.

items.title: feat(tools): load local user tool plugins from PINCH_TOOLS_DIR with approval gating
items.body:
## Context

`docs/CAPABILITIES.json` (`plugin-api`) and Growth issue #37 note that adding a custom local tool without spinning up an MCP server currently requires editing `src/tools.js`.

## What to change

- `src/tools.js`: support optional `PINCH_TOOLS_DIR` loading `.js`/`.mjs` tool modules via `registerTool()`, defaulting `dangerous: true` (requires in-chat approval) unless explicitly trusted, and refusing to shadow built-in tools.
- `docs/GUIDE.md` & `test/tools.test.js`: document the 15-line plugin contract and test shadowing refusal + approval-gate default.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] User tool modules register cleanly via `registerTool()` without modifying `src/tools.js`
- [ ] Untrusted plugin tools default to `dangerous: true` (approval required) and cannot shadow built-ins
- [ ] Tested in `test/tools.test.js` and passes `node scripts/audit.js`

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/tools.test.js
node scripts/audit.js
```

## Time estimate

~3-4 hours.

items.title: feat(rag): zero-dependency BM25 workspace document index with validated citations
items.body:
## Context

`docs/CAPABILITIES.json` (`rag-documents`) and Growth issue #39 highlight local document indexing & Q&A. Pinch can index Markdown, text, PDF, and DOCX files inside `PINCH_WORKSPACE` using pure-JS BM25 chunk ranking and `src/attachments.js` extractors — zero native or cloud dependencies.

## What to change

- Add incremental mtime-keyed BM25 chunk indexing confined via `resolveInWorkspace()`.
- Register every retrieved passage in `src/sources.js` so `src/citations.js` and `src/guard.js` validate `[n]` citations identically to web and file reads.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Strictly confined to `PINCH_WORKSPACE` (`realpath` checked, symlink escapes refused)
- [ ] Retrieved passages register in `src/sources.js` so invented `[n]` citations still trigger `guard.js`
- [ ] Zero new runtime dependencies; passes `node --test` and `node scripts/audit.js`

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/citations.test.js test/tools.test.js
node scripts/audit.js
```

## Time estimate

~4-5 hours.
